input.text: Fayuan is the oldest temple in inner Beijing — founded in the Tang dynasty in six forty-five by the emperor Taizong, mourning soldiers lost in a disastrous Korean campaign; it was called the Temple for Comforting the Loyal before gaining its present name, "the Source of Buddhist Law." Over thirteen centuries, it has been a prison, a poetry salon, a seminary — today it houses the Chinese Buddhist Academy, and young monks still study in its courtyards. The temple is loved in spring, when its famous lilacs bloom and poets have gathered under them for centuries; the writer Li Ao's novel about the temple made it famous far beyond Beijing. Statues range from a giant seated Buddha to bronze pieces centuries apart. Hidden in the hutongs near the Muslim quarter, it sees few tourists — come at reading hour, when chanting rolls softly across courtyards of ancient trees, and thirteen hundred years sit very lightly on one small temple.
